description: Standalone flash overlay loaded on top of skills_ii_target_miss_solutions_added(90skills).json (or 73-skills base for no-avoids variants). NOT merged into the packaged library. Runtime: C2HLS_PACKAGED_SKILLS_JSON + C2HLS_FLASH_SKILL_ENTRIES_JSON.

skills.pattern: any flash kernel with nested loops, PIPELINE pragmas, m_axi load/store, reductions, triangular/variable bounds, or DATAFLOW regions
skills.strategy: Before final code, audit every loop nest: (1) bounds; (2) compile-time constant vs variable trip count; (3) subloops in body; (4) reductions/accumulations; (5) m_axi reads/writes; (6) legal/realistic pipeline location. Reject and revise if anti-patterns remain. After code generation, emit an audit table: loop name | original issue | applied transformation | pipeline pragma location | remaining II risk | memory-port risk.
required_steps: enumerate every loop nest and record bounds, trip-count kind, subloops, reductions, and m_axi touch
verify pipeline pragma is only on innermost legal loop (or parent with fully-unrolled/flattened children only)
rewrite variable-bound loops (k<i, k<j, j>i+1, i<tile_size) to fixed TILE_SIZE/N loops with if guards
split FP reductions into private partial accumulators with complete partition, then final reduction
pipeline innermost contiguous memory copy loops only — never outer row/tile loops over full N columns
keep m_axi as load-compute-store: no inner-loop RMW on m_axi ports
match ARRAY_PARTITION to unroll factor and parallel port needs
use canonical DATAFLOW: declarations and function calls only inside the region
do not add ping-pong or DATAFLOW unless producer-consumer overlap is real — report overlap or remove
reject code with any listed anti-pattern and revise before submitting
produce the final loop audit table in the response
guards: LOOP_TRIPCOUNT is reporting only — it does not make loops statically bounded
partial UNROLL factor>1 still leaves a child loop — parent PIPELINE II=1 is illegal unless child is fully unrolled
do not rely on LOOP_FLATTEN alone to fix variable-trip nests
preserve numerical semantics when adding guards or partial accumulators
skills.template:
AUDIT TABLE (required):
| loop | original issue | transformation | pipeline location | II risk | memory-port risk |

ANTI-PATTERNS (reject if present):
- parent pipelined with non-fully-unrolled child
- variable-trip child under pipelined parent
- partial unroll treated as full unroll
- scalar FP recurrence in claimed II=1 loop
- outer memory-copy loop pipelined over full row
- direct RMW on m_axi inside compute loops

skills.pattern: #pragma HLS PIPELINE II=1 on a parent loop whose body contains another loop that is not fully unrolled (including UNROLL factor=N partial unroll)
skills.strategy: Do not pipeline the parent when a child loop still exists. Partial unroll is not full unroll. Pipeline only the innermost loop, fully unroll the child, or use an explicitly flattenable nest — never assume LOOP_FLATTEN fixes a variable or partially-unrolled child.
required_steps: detect parent PIPELINE pragma with a nested for-loop in the body
check whether every child loop is fully unrolled or the nest is provably flattenable
if any child loop remains, move PIPELINE to innermost legal loop or fully unroll child
do not treat UNROLL factor=4 as removing the child loop
guards: LOOP_FLATTEN does not substitute for full unroll when bounds are variable
validate II on the actual pipelined loop after moving pragmas

skills.pattern: variable-trip-count loops (triangular, tile_size, k<i, k<j, j=i+1..N) fixed only with LOOP_TRIPCOUNT or LOOP_FLATTEN without rewriting to static bounds
skills.strategy: LOOP_TRIPCOUNT is for reporting/estimation only — it does not make a loop statically bounded, fully unrollable, or dependency-free. Do not rely on LOOP_FLATTEN or LOOP_TRIPCOUNT to legalize pipeline on variable-bound nests.
required_steps: identify loops whose bound depends on an outer induction variable or runtime tile_size
do not add LOOP_TRIPCOUNT as a substitute for static bounds
rewrite to fixed-bound loops with if guards using N or TILE_SIZE constants
re-validate pipeline legality on the rewritten nest
guards: preserve original semantics with if (idx < bound) guards
use header macro constants for fixed bounds

skills.pattern: triangular or variable-bound loops such as for (k=0; k<i), for (k=0; k<j), for (j=i+1; j<N), or for (i=0; i<tile_size) blocking II=1 pipeline
skills.strategy: Rewrite to fixed compile-time bounds (N, TILE_SIZE from header macros) and preserve semantics with if guards on the induction variable.
required_steps: replace runtime or outer-dependent bounds with fixed TILE_SIZE or N
wrap body in if (idx < original_bound) to skip out-of-range iterations
apply PIPELINE II=1 only on the fixed-bound inner loop after rewrite
keep tile_size as a scalar for guard comparisons, not as the loop bound when pipelining
guards: do not change numerical results — guards must match original iteration set
prefer TILE_SIZE macro over function parameter for synthesizable bounds

skills.pattern: floating-point reduction or accumulation into one scalar inside a loop claimed II=1 (e.g. w -= a*b, sum += expr, acc = acc + expr as the only accumulation chain)
skills.strategy: Do not accumulate into a single scalar inside a pipelined loop. Use private partial accumulators with complete ARRAY_PARTITION, unrolled init/update, then a final tree or serial reduction.
required_steps: detect FP update statements that read and write the same scalar accumulator in the pipelined loop
allocate partial[UF] with complete partition
unroll init and per-lane updates inside pipelined fixed-bound loops
reduce partial[] after the pipelined loop
guards: choose UF to match available DSP/budget
preserve numerics within acceptable reordering for independent partials

skills.pattern: floating-point dot-product, sum, or coupled update (w -= a*b) inside a loop targeted for II=1
skills.strategy: Use UF private partial accumulators with complete partition; unrolled init; pipelined fixed-bound loop with unrolled lane updates and guards; final reduction of partial[] into result scalar.
required_steps: const int UF = 4; double partial[UF]; #pragma HLS ARRAY_PARTITION variable=partial complete
unrolled init of partial[p] = 0
outer pipelined loop steps by UF over fixed TILE_SIZE bound
inner unrolled lane updates partial[p] with guarded index
after loop, sum partial[] into output scalar or local
guards: only use when lane iterations are independent
match UF to unroll factor and memory ports

skills.pattern: memory load/store tile loops with #pragma HLS PIPELINE II=1 on the outer row/tile loop (for i) while an inner loop iterates all N columns per outer step
skills.strategy: Pipeline the innermost contiguous memory loop only. Do not ask HLS to load or store an entire matrix row per pipeline cycle. Outer i loops should be sequential; inner j loop gets PIPELINE II=1.
required_steps: find load_tile/store_tile nests pipelining the outer i loop
remove PIPELINE from outer loop over tile rows
move PIPELINE II=1 to innermost j loop over contiguous elements
keep scalar row loads (b[i], y[i]) outside or after the inner pipelined j loop
guards: pair with local buffers so inner loop touches BRAM not m_axi when possible
one element per pipeline iteration for m_axi when pipelining global access

skills.pattern: tile load/store phases copying between m_axi ports and local buffers with nested i-j loops
skills.strategy: Structure load_tile and store_tile as outer sequential row/tile loops with innermost pipelined contiguous copy loop over j (or flat index). Scalar vector loads/stores (b[i], y[i]) execute once per row outside the pipelined inner loop.
required_steps: outer loop: for i over TILE_SIZE or fixed tile rows — no PIPELINE on outer
inner loop: for j over N — #pragma HLS PIPELINE II=1 on inner only
load local_A[i][j] from A[tile_i+i][j] in inner pipelined loop
load local_b[i] from b[tile_i+i] after inner j loop completes for row i
mirror structure for store_tile
guards: use if (tile_i+i < N) guards when tile tail is partial
local arrays should be BRAM with bounds from header macros

skills.pattern: UNROLL by factor UF on a loop that reads/writes local arrays without enough parallel memory ports
skills.strategy: Apply ARRAY_PARTITION (cyclic or complete) so local arrays expose enough read/write ports for the unroll factor. Complete partition for small partial-sum arrays; cyclic factor=UF for lane buffers.
required_steps: identify unroll factor UF on hot loop
count simultaneous array accesses per unrolled iteration
add #pragma HLS ARRAY_PARTITION with factor matching UF or complete for small arrays
verify csynth does not report memory port conflicts on locals
guards: watch BRAM/LUT growth from complete partition on large arrays
partition dim must match access pattern (row vs column)

skills.pattern: DATAFLOW region containing complex if/else, non-unit loop increments, or dynamic control logic instead of declarations and function calls
skills.strategy: Use canonical DATAFLOW regions: stream/buffer declarations and calls to load/compute/store subfunctions only. Move control logic, boundary handling, and non-unit loops outside or into subfunctions called from the dataflow region.
required_steps: split load, compute, store into separate functions
inside #pragma HLS DATAFLOW: declare hls::stream or ping-pong buffers and call subfunctions
move if/else tile guards into subfunctions or use bounded canonical loops
no non-unit stride loops or dynamic allocation inside the dataflow region
guards: subfunctions must be synthesizable with stable interfaces
fifo depths must cover producer-consumer latency

skills.pattern: kernel uses or proposes #pragma HLS DATAFLOW, ping-pong buffers, or double-buffered tile staging
skills.strategy: Do not add ping-pong buffers or DATAFLOW unless the code expresses a valid canonical producer-consumer schedule with real overlap. Default to single local buffer + pipelined load/compute/store loops when true cross-tile overlap is not implemented.
required_steps: audit every DATAFLOW region: only declarations and function calls — no if/else, dynamic tile math, or non-unit increments inside
use unit-increment tile index: for (tile=0; tile<NUM_TILES; tile++) with tile_i = tile * TILE_SIZE — never DATAFLOW inside tile_i += TILE_SIZE
reject ping-pong that only alternates buffers across sequential tile iterations without load(t+1) overlapping compute/store(t)
for triangular factorization/solve or other cross-tile dependencies, prove tile overlap is legal before ping-pong or DATAFLOW across tiles
factor load-compute-store DATAFLOW into a helper with load_fn(); compute_fn(); store_fn(); calls only
if no true overlap, use one local buffer and fix loop II, memory access, and reductions first
report whether ping-pong provides actual overlap; if not, remove ping-pong and DATAFLOW
guards: decorative DATAFLOW/ping-pong wastes BRAM and can block II fixes
fifo/stream depths must match real producer-consumer latency when overlap exists
sequential tile processing with cross-tile deps forbids fake overlap
skills.template:
OVERLAP REPORT (required if ping-pong/DATAFLOW present):
| stage pairing | overlap? | evidence |

BAD: sequential tiles with buf[tile&1] but no concurrent load/compute
GOOD: #pragma HLS DATAFLOW + load_tile(t+1) || compute_tile(t) with proven independence

skills.pattern: #pragma HLS DATAFLOW placed inside a tile loop using non-unit increment such as for (tile_i = 0; tile_i < N; tile_i += TILE_SIZE)
skills.strategy: Do not place DATAFLOW inside tile_i += TILE_SIZE loops. Use a unit-increment tile index and compute the base offset outside the dataflow region.
required_steps: detect DATAFLOW pragma nested under tile_i += TILE_SIZE or similar non-unit outer loop
replace with for (int tile = 0; tile < NUM_TILES; tile++) and tile_i = tile * TILE_SIZE
move #pragma HLS DATAFLOW to a helper called once per tile with canonical load/compute/store calls
keep dynamic tail handling inside subfunctions, not as control flow inside the DATAFLOW region
guards: NUM_TILES = (N + TILE_SIZE - 1) / TILE_SIZE must be compile-time friendly
last partial tile handled inside load/compute/store functions with guards

skills.pattern: ping-pong or double buffers (buf[2], tile&1, in_buf/out_buf alternation) across sequential tile iterations without load of tile t+1 overlapping compute or store of tile t
skills.strategy: Ping-pong is valid only when load of tile t+1 overlaps compute/store of tile t, or a clearly defined multi-stage dataflow pipeline overlaps independent tiles. If tiles run strictly sequentially with no concurrent stages, use a single local buffer.
required_steps: identify ping-pong buffer indexing (tile % 2, buf[0]/buf[1], in_ping/in_pong)
verify concurrent producer-consumer schedule: while computing tile t, loading tile t+1 (or storing t-1)
if stages still run serially per tile, remove ping-pong and use one local_A/local_b buffer
prioritize inner-loop II=1, memory copy placement, and reduction fixes before re-adding overlap
state in the response whether ping-pong provides actual overlap; remove if it does not
guards: doubling local BRAM without overlap increases resource pressure with no throughput gain
alternating buffer indices alone does not create hardware overlap

skills.pattern: triangular factorization, triangular solve, or other pivot-dependent tiled algorithms using ping-pong or DATAFLOW tile overlap without proving cross-tile dependence safety
skills.strategy: Algorithms with cross-tile dependencies (especially triangular factorization or solve with pivot-dependent active regions) require a dependence proof before overlapping tiles. Default to sequential tiles with local staging; do not assume ping-pong is legal.
required_steps: identify cross-tile read-after-write or triangular dependencies (pivot row, active column, forward substitution)
reject ping-pong/DATAFLOW across tiles unless dependence analysis shows independence
process dependent tiles sequentially; overlap only separate load/compute/store stages within one tile via canonical DATAFLOW if legal
document dependence reasoning when proposing any tile overlap
guards: numerical correctness overrides throughput — wrong overlap breaks triangular factorization/solve
pivot-dependent active regions make arbitrary tile overlap unsafe

skills.pattern: load-compute-store tiling where DATAFLOW overlap between stages is desired and tile dependencies permit concurrent stages
skills.strategy: Factor each tile into a helper function whose body is a canonical DATAFLOW region containing only buffer/stream declarations plus exactly three calls: load function, compute function, store function.
required_steps: define load_tile, compute_tile, store_tile as separate synthesizable functions
helper process_tile_lcs contains #pragma HLS DATAFLOW with declarations + three calls only
outer host loop uses unit tile index; compute tile_i = tile * TILE_SIZE before calling helper
no if/else, dynamic tile calculations, or non-unit increments inside the DATAFLOW region
verify overlap report: concurrent stages, not merely alternating buffer names
guards: use hls::stream or ping-pong locals only when fifo depth covers stage latency
skip DATAFLOW entirely if stages cannot overlap — use pipelined sequential phases

skills.pattern: matrix-vector or dot-product style loops that update an output accumulator array element inside a pipelined and/or unrolled loop (e.g. local_x[i] += expr under #pragma HLS PIPELINE II=1 or UNROLL over column index j+k)
skills.strategy: Never read-modify-write the same local output accumulator element inside a pipelined unrolled loop. Use private partial accumulators with complete partitioning, reduce once after the pipelined loop, then assign local_x[i] exactly once.
required_steps: detect local_x[i] += or equivalent in-place update inside PIPELINE II=1 or unrolled j+k loops
allocate partial[UF] per output lane or per unroll lane with #pragma HLS ARRAY_PARTITION complete
accumulate into partial[p] inside the pipelined/unrolled loop
reduce partial[] to a scalar after the loop and write local_x[i] once
do not leave loop-carried dependence on local_x[i] in the hot pipeline
guards: applies to local staging buffers as well as m_axi outputs — same RMW discipline
pair with hls-fp-reduction-partial-accumulators for FP dot-product chains
preserve numerical semantics when splitting partial sums

skills.pattern: matrix-vector multiply or dot-product inner loop unrolled over column index j+k accessing matrix row i and vector y[j+k]
skills.strategy: When unrolling over column index j+k, explicitly partition the matrix along the column dimension and partition the vector along its only dimension. Do not rely on HLS to infer missing partitions.
required_steps: set UF unroll factor on the j+k column loop
add #pragma HLS ARRAY_PARTITION on matrix A cyclic or complete on dim=2 (columns) with factor=UF
add #pragma HLS ARRAY_PARTITION on vector y cyclic factor=UF dim=1
verify csynth reports no local memory port conflicts on the unrolled accesses
match partition factors to the actual UNROLL factor on j+k
guards: complete partition only when column/vector slice is small
row-major A[i][j+k] needs column-dim partition for simultaneous j+k reads

skills.pattern: algorithm needs both row-major and column-oriented (transposed) local views of the same matrix for matrix-vector or multi-phase compute
skills.strategy: Load the matrix from m_axi once and populate both normal and transposed local buffers from the same external read stream. Do not read the full matrix twice from m_axi unless explicitly required by correctness.
required_steps: identify phases that need A[i][j] and A[j][i] or column-slice vs row-slice access
single pipelined load loop: read A[i][j] from m_axi once per element
write the value into row-major local_A[i][j] and transposed local_AT[j][i] in the same iteration
run compute from locals only — no second full-matrix m_axi load
store outputs once after local finalize
guards: on-chip BRAM budget must fit both layouts or tile the shared load
transposed layout indexing must match compute access pattern
const m_axi inputs: one read per element per logical load pass

skills.pattern: compute loops perform read-modify-write updates directly on arrays mapped to m_axi ports (e.g. A[i][j] = A[i][j] + expr, x[i] = x[i] + expr, w[i] = w[i] + expr inside nested loops)
skills.strategy: Treat every m_axi argument as external DRAM/HBM. Never read and write the same external element inside an inner loop. Do not use global/m_axi arrays as temporary storage or assume HLS will cache m_axi data across iterations.
required_steps: scan every loop for statements that read and write the same m_axi port element
reject direct accumulation into m_axi arrays
reject repeated reads of the same output element from DRAM/HBM inside an inner loop
reject repeated writes to the same output element inside an inner loop
replace with load-compute-store using local buffers or private scalar accumulators
for reductions, accumulate in a private scalar or local array, then write back once
if the full array is too large, tile/block but still finalize each tile locally before one store
guards: preserve numerical semantics when staging into locals
const read-only m_axi inputs may be read once per tile into locals
in-place outputs still require local write-back buffers, not inner-loop RMW on the port

skills.pattern: kernel touches m_axi pointer ports in compute loops and may benefit from pipelining, unroll, or DATAFLOW but must not bottleneck on repeated external memory RMW
skills.strategy: Use explicit load-compute-store: (1) load required inputs from m_axi into local on-chip buffers or private scalars; (2) perform all repeated updates, reductions, and accumulations on locals only; (3) store final results back to m_axi outputs once per element when possible. Prefer burst-friendly sequential loads/stores and separate phases.
required_steps: identify every m_axi port used in compute
add local buffers for reused arrays and private scalar accumulators for reductions
pipeline load, compute, and store loops independently where legal
write each output m_axi element at most once per logical update (after local finalize)
apply tiling when full arrays exceed on-chip budget while keeping RMW off m_axi inside inner loops
guards: do not change top-level pointer element types unless explicitly allowed
pair with distinct gmemN bundles per port when parallelizing external access
local arrays must be sized with fixed bounds from header macros

skills.pattern: kernel has two or more m_axi pointer ports and uses #pragma HLS DATAFLOW or multiple load/compute/store tasks that should overlap external memory access
skills.strategy: Assign a distinct bundle=gmem0, gmem1, … to each m_axi pointer port so HLS can issue concurrent external memory transactions across DATAFLOW stages. Never place all read/write ports on a single bundle=gmem when stages are meant to run concurrently.
required_steps: enumerate every m_axi port on the top kernel and on DATAFLOW subfunctions that touch global memory
assign each pointer port a unique bundle=gmemN (gmem0, gmem1, gmem2, …)
map load tasks to read ports and store tasks to write ports on separate bundles when stages overlap
re-run csynth and verify parallel tasks no longer stall on a single gmem port (HLS 200-885 on gmem)
pair with hls::stream or proven stage overlap — distinct bundles alone do not fix decorative DATAFLOW
guards: each bundle still needs burst-friendly access patterns on its port
do not duplicate bundle names across unrelated ports
cosim and interface pragmas must stay consistent after rebundling
skills.template:
// BAD: all ports share one bundle — DATAFLOW tasks serialize on gmem
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=A bundle=gmem
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=B bundle=gmem
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=y bundle=gmem

// GOOD: one bundle per port for concurrent stage access
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=A bundle=gmem0
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=B bundle=gmem1
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=y bundle=gmem2

skills.pattern: #pragma HLS DATAFLOW wrapping multiple tasks that communicate only through shared local arrays or caller globals (no hls::stream, no ping-pong with proven overlap) while all m_axi ports use one bundle=gmem
skills.strategy: In the DATAFLOW refactor step, always keep `#pragma HLS DATAFLOW`. Prove producer–consumer overlap with hls::stream FIFOs, distinct gmemN bundles per port, or ping-pong buffers — fix structure until overlap is real. Never omit DATAFLOW or revert to sequential load → compute → store without the pragma.
required_steps: inspect every DATAFLOW region: list tasks, how data moves between them, and whether hls::stream or distinct bundles exist
reject task graphs where multiple concurrent tasks write the same local array without ping-pong or streams
reject parallel per-port loaders on shared bundle=gmem — rebundle to gmem0/gmem1/... first
require an overlap report (stage pairing | overlap? | evidence) and fix gaps with gmemN, streams, or ping-pong
never remove #pragma HLS DATAFLOW in this step — repair task boundaries instead
if ap_ctrl_none is used with DATAFLOW, prefer ap_ctrl_chain or fix task interfaces to avoid deadlock (HLS 200-656)
guards: increasing FIFO depth (HLS 200-1019/1020) is not a substitute for real overlap
tasks must not read caller m_axi arrays directly while also having a DATAFLOW predecessor (HLS 200-1449)
decorative multi-task DATAFLOW often loses to flash-selected sequential pipelined code

skills.pattern: single load task pipelines the outer row loop for multiple large matrices in sequence (matrix A, then B, then C…) each with #pragma HLS PIPELINE II=1 on the outer i loop
skills.strategy: Split per-matrix load into its own function with innermost pipelined dimension only, or fuse into one flat index loop over all elements. Do not stack multiple outer-pipelined row loops in one task — each outer pipeline asks HLS to move an entire row per cycle and serializes memory ports.
required_steps: detect load functions that outer-pipeline for (i) over rows for more than one large array
remove PIPELINE from outer row loops; pipeline innermost contiguous index (j or flat idx) only
prefer separate load_matrix_A / load_matrix_B helpers or one fused flat load loop
if parallel load tasks are needed, pair each with distinct gmemN bundles and DATAFLOW overlap proof
verify csynth II on hot copy loop — not inflated outer-row pipeline
guards: pair with hls-pipeline-innermost-memory-copy-loop for each matrix
scalar vector loads (b[i]) stay outside inner pipelined j loop
partial final tile uses TILE_SIZE bound + if guards, not runtime tile_size as loop bound

skills.pattern: chained matrix multiplies (output = alpha * A*B + beta * … with multiple GEMM stages) implemented with multiple full-size local temporaries and extra copy loops between stages
skills.strategy: Reuse minimal local tile or K-panel accumulators; pipeline the K dimension innermost with ARRAY_PARTITION on the K access dimension; avoid allocating local_tmp1/local_tmp2/local_tmp3 full-matrix buffers and copy tasks between GEMM stages. Prefer one compute nest per tile or stream K-panels between stages via hls::stream when DATAFLOW overlap is real.
required_steps: identify GEMM chain depth and which intermediates must persist vs can be streamed
allocate the smallest local buffers that cover one tile or one K-panel, not full N×N per stage
pipeline innermost K loop with II=1; partition locals on K/column dim to match unroll
remove redundant matrix-to-matrix copy loops between DATAFLOW tasks

if one local buffer (e.g. tmp) is consumed by two downstream tasks (second GEMM + store), insert hls::stream or duplicate buffer with single-writer/single-reader chain — never one writer + two concurrent readers (HLS 200-779)
add DATAFLOW between GEMM stages only with hls::stream panel FIFOs and overlap report
fold alpha/beta scaling into the same local accumulator where numerically legal
guards: on-chip BRAM budget may require tiling — reuse tiles, not duplicate full matrices
preserve numerical semantics when reordering multiply-add chains
do not add decorative multi-task DATAFLOW without streams — see avoid-dataflow-without-stream-or-overlap-proof

skills.pattern: pipelined load_tile, compute_tile, or store_tile loops use for (i = 0; i < tile_size; i++) where tile_size is runtime-computed for the final partial tile
skills.strategy: Loop bound must be compile-time TILE_SIZE from header macros; use if (tile_i + i < N) guards for partial final tile. Runtime tile_size as loop bound blocks II=1 pipeline, UNROLL, and LOOP_FLATTEN (HLS 200-936/960).
required_steps: replace for (i = 0; i < tile_size; i++) with for (i = 0; i < TILE_SIZE; i++)
guard loads, stores, and compute with if (tile_i + i < N) or if (i < tile_size) only inside body — not as loop bound
keep tile_size scalar for guard comparisons when needed, not as pipelined loop trip count
re-apply PIPELINE II=1 on inner fixed-bound loops after rewrite
validate csynth no longer warns cannot unroll/flatten due to variable tile_size bound
guards: TILE_SIZE macro must match tiling pragma and local buffer allocation
preserve semantics for partial tail tile — skipped iterations must not change results
complements hls-rewrite-variable-trip-fixed-bound-guard for triangular inner bounds

skills.pattern: tiled load/compute/store phase reads x[gi] from m_axi, accumulates into local_x[i], then writes x[gi] back within the same tile iteration — per-tile RMW on external port
skills.strategy: Load the output vector into local memory once (or hold per-element local state across tiles), accumulate entirely in local memory until all contributions for that element are complete, then perform a single store per output element to m_axi.
required_steps: detect per-tile patterns: load x[global_i] → local_x[i] += expr → store x[global_i]
replace with load full or partial x into local_x once before tiled compute, or keep local_x across tile loop without per-tile m_axi writeback
accumulate in local_x[i] or private scalar during compute tiles only
write each m_axi output element once after all tiles that touch that element have finished
if output is too large for one local buffer, tile outputs with local finalize per tile region — still no inner-tile m_axi RMW
guards: extends avoid-no-rmw-m_axi-direct to tiled staging specifically
const m_axi inputs may still be loaded per tile; in-place outputs need local write-back discipline
preserve numerical semantics when deferring store to end of tile sequence

skills.pattern: one local array written by a compute task and read by two or more concurrent DATAFLOW tasks (e.g. compute stage + store stage + downstream compute all touch local_tmp)
skills.strategy: Every local array in a DATAFLOW region must have exactly one writer task and exactly one reader task. For fan-out (one producer, multiple consumers), chain with hls::stream FIFOs, duplicate into separate single-use buffers (buf_for_compute / buf_for_store), or merge consumers into one task.
required_steps: list every local array and mark writer task + reader task
reject any local with >1 writer or >1 concurrent reader
if compute writes local_M and both store and a later compute read local_M, insert hls::stream between producer and each consumer OR serialize store after final consumer in a linear chain
for load→compute handoff use buf_in written only by load, read only by compute; compute writes buf_out read only by store
re-run csynth until HLS 200-779 / 200-979 are gone
guards: ping-pong buf0/buf1 still obeys one writer per bank per time step
hls::stream depth ≥ 2 when producer may run ahead of consumer
do not pass the same local array into three task calls under one #pragma HLS DATAFLOW

skills.pattern: #pragma HLS DATAFLOW wrapping a for (t = 0; t < TSTEPS; t++) loop that calls alternating compute tasks which read/write the same local arrays (stencil time steps, iterative relaxation)
skills.strategy: Temporal iteration (tsteps, time loops) belongs inside a single compute task, not as multiple concurrent DATAFLOW tasks in an outer t-loop. Use ping-pong locals (A_in/A_out or buf0/buf1) inside that one compute task for alternating read/write phases.
required_steps: detect outer t-loop or phase-loop inside #pragma HLS DATAFLOW
move the entire t-loop into one static compute_* task with INLINE off
use separate local arrays for alternating phases (local_A, local_B, local_A_new) — each array has one writer per iteration inside the compute task
keep DATAFLOW as load_task → compute_all_timesteps_task → store_task only
never call compute_phase_A and compute_phase_B as sibling tasks under DATAFLOW inside a shared t-loop
guards: fixes HLS 200-979 'can only be written in one process' on stencil locals
DATAFLOW overlap is load || compute || store, not per-timestep task parallelism
label inner t-loop and phase loops for audit

skills.pattern: for (tile = 0; tile < NUM_TILES; tile++) loop placed inside #pragma HLS DATAFLOW calling load tasks that read the same m_axi port each iteration — HLS instantiates parallel readers on one bundle (HLS 200-1013 / 200-984)
skills.strategy: Never put a tile-indexed for-loop inside #pragma HLS DATAFLOW if the loop body calls tasks that read/write m_axi ports. Either: (1) fuse all tile loads into one task with pipelined inner loops, (2) move the tile loop outside DATAFLOW into a helper that calls a per-tile DATAFLOW body with private buffers, or (3) use hls::stream tile pipeline (load_tile→compute_tile→store_tile) with depth≥2.
required_steps: detect for (i0 = 0; i0 < N; i0 += TILE_SIZE) inside #pragma HLS DATAFLOW
if body calls load_* tasks touching m_axi, refactor to single fused load OR stream pipeline
each m_axi port: at most one concurrent reader and one concurrent writer across DATAFLOW tasks
for multi-phase kernels (two passes over same matrix), preload full matrix into locals in one task before phased compute
verify csynth no longer reports bundled bus interface read in multiple processes
guards: distinct gmemN per port does not fix multiple concurrent readers on the same port
pair with hls-single-load-dual-local-layout when one matrix needs two access patterns
ARRAY_PARTITION local tile buffers for compute parallelism after fused load

skills.pattern: DATAFLOW structure passes csynth but latency is high because compute tasks lack ARRAY_PARTITION, inner UNROLL, and parallel load/store overlap
skills.strategy: After correct DATAFLOW task boundaries, maximize throughput: partition local arrays on the inner compute dimension, UNROLL inner loops to match partition factor, pipeline innermost loops II=1, run independent load tasks in parallel on distinct gmemN bundles, and use hls::stream depth 4–16 for tile pipelines to overlap load(t+1) with compute(t).
required_steps: add #pragma HLS ARRAY_PARTITION cyclic or block on hot local arrays — factor matches UNROLL
add #pragma HLS UNROLL factor=UF on innermost reduction/dot-product loop
pipeline innermost memory/compute loop with II=1; never outer row loop PIPELINE for multi-matrix loads
issue parallel load tasks only when each touches a different m_axi port/bundle
for tiled kernels use hls::stream tile FIFO between load_tile, compute_tile, store_tile for real overlap
target higher DSP/FF utilization when latency slack exists — prefer parallelism over minimal resources
guards: partition/unroll must not break DATAFLOW buffer ownership rules
BRAM budget: tile smaller or stream panels instead of full-matrix locals
complements hls-array-partition-match-unroll-factor from base skills

skills.pattern: multiple compute tasks under #pragma HLS DATAFLOW each read the same local array (matrix reused in two GEMMs, dual matvec on same A, or stat pipeline mean→stddev→normalize all touching local_data) — HLS 200-779
skills.strategy: Merge every compute phase that shares a local input or intermediate into ONE static compute_fused_task with sequential labeled loops inside. Keep parallel load_* and store_* as separate DATAFLOW tasks. Never add an inline for-loop copy inside DATAFLOW to dodge fan-out — that creates another reader process.
required_steps: list compute tasks and mark which locals each reads/writes
if two+ compute tasks read the same local (e.g. local_A, local_data_in, local_tmp): fold into one compute_fused_task
if one intermediate is consumed by downstream compute AND store_tmp: either store inside the fused compute after last use, or chain linearly compute_fused → local_out read only by store
for chained GEMMs (tmp = alpha*A*B; D = beta*D + tmp*C): one task does both nests sequentially; parallel loads for A,B,C,D_in; parallel stores for tmp and D_out only after fused compute completes
for dual matvec (tmp=A*x; y=A'*tmp): one task reads local_A once for both phases
for stat pipelines (mean, stddev, normalize, corr): one compute_stats_task with sequential loops; parallel store_mean/store_stddev/store_corr OK after
guards: fused compute task must not take m_axi port pointers
do not place copy loops inside DATAFLOW region — use separate copy task or fuse into compute
preserve numerical order when merging phases

skills.pattern: kernel runs two passes over the same matrix with different access (row-major then transposed/column) and places tile for-loops inside #pragma HLS DATAFLOW that call load_* on the same m_axi port each iteration — HLS 200-1013
skills.strategy: Under DATAFLOW: one fused_load_task reads the matrix from m_axi once per element and fills both row-major and transposed local buffers in the same pipelined loop; load all vectors in the same or parallel tasks; run phase1_task and phase2_task on locals only; fused_store_task for outputs. No outer tile loop inside DATAFLOW that touches m_axi.
required_steps: replace per-tile load loops inside DATAFLOW with single fused_load_task covering full N×N (or legal tile stream pipeline with hls::stream, not repeated m_axi loads)
in fused load: for each (i,j) read A[i][j] once; write local_A_row[i][j] and local_A_col[j][i]
phase1_task uses local_A_row; phase2_task uses local_A_col — no m_axi in either
optional ARRAY_PARTITION on row locals for UNROLL in compute
verify no HLS 200-1013 on matrix port
guards: BRAM must fit both layouts — partition/unroll compute not load
pair with hls-single-load-dual-local-layout
distinct gmemN on vector ports enables parallel y1/y2 loads with fused A load

skills.pattern: two compute tasks under #pragma HLS DATAFLOW both read the same local array produced by an upstream task (e.g. compute_x and compute_w both consume local_A_out) — HLS 200-779
skills.strategy: Merge the parallel consumer compute tasks into one compute_xw_task with sequential labeled loops, or insert hls::stream between producer and a single downstream consumer. Never leave two concurrent reader tasks on the same local buffer.
required_steps: identify locals with one writer and two+ reader compute tasks
merge consumers into one static task with both computation nests inside
if merge hurts II, use hls::stream from producer to one consumer and duplicate producer output via second stream (tee) — never two tasks reading same local
tile loops wrapping DATAFLOW: each tile iteration must use private tile buffers; still no fan-out within one DATAFLOW invocation
guards: merged task stays locals-only — no m_axi pointers
store tasks may run parallel only if each reads a distinct local output
